title: Grafting immunity: jasmonate and raffinose on the move
content: Grafting is a technique that has been used for centuries to combine desirable traits in food crops and other horticultural plants. After successfully joining shoot (scion) and root (rootstock), the 2 plant parts (scion–rootstock) establish vascular continuity, and subsequently continue to grow as one plant (Melnyk and Meyerowitz 2015; Kragler and Bock 2025). In modern horticulture, grafting is widely used to enhance plant tolerance to environmental stresses and diseases (Zhang et al. 2022). However, the molecular mechanisms through which the communication between rootstock and scion confers resistance to pathogen infection remain poorly understood.
